summary: The Federal Reserve's Supervision and Regulation section of the 2024 Annual Report provides comprehensive data on the U.S. banking sector structure. As of December 31, 2024, the Fed supervised 3,408 community banking organizations (total assets under $10B), 105 regional banking organizations ($10B-$100B), and 172 large/foreign banking organizations ($100B+). Bank holding companies control approximately 95% of all insured commercial bank assets. The report details oversight of financial market utilities, supervised insurance organizations (5 firms with ~$450B in total assets), and the risk-based supervision framework.
why_it_matters: This official Federal Reserve document provides authoritative baseline data on the structure of the U.S. banking system, including the distribution of assets across institution categories and the regulatory landscape. It serves as a reference point for understanding systemic risk, market concentration, and the scope of Federal Reserve supervisory authority.
macro_context: The data reflects the post-2023 banking stress environment, with updated statistics on bank holding companies (3,747 total), financial holding companies (497 domestic FHCs as of year-end 2025), and the supervisory framework. The LISCC (Large Institution Supervision Coordinating Committee) oversees eight U.S. G-SIBs with $15.2 trillion in combined assets.
market_structure_context: The Federal Reserve supervises a tiered structure of banking organizations from community banks ($3.0T total assets) through regional institutions ($4.2T) to large banking organizations including systemically important institutions ($15.2T under LISCC). This supervisory structure is fundamental to understanding banking market dynamics, concentration risk, and the transmission of monetary policy through the financial system.
